ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two bamboo poles $AB$ and $DB$ are leaning against the wall $CE$ at angles such that $\angle CAB = 33^\circ$ and $\angle CDB = 21^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle CAB$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABD$ and $\angle CAB=33^\circ$, $\angle CDB=21^\circ$,\\
then $\angle CAB=\angle ABD+\angle CDB$,\\
thus, $\angle ABD=\angle CAB-\angle CDB=12^\circ$,\\
therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{12^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Form triangle ABD from the two bamboo poles and the segment AD of the wall. From the image, A and D are on the same straight wall, with C below A, so rays AC and AD are opposite rays. Therefore the interior angle at A of triangle ABD is angle DAB = 180° - angle CAB = 180° - 33° = 147°.
